design_rationales.concrete_problem: Repeated interaction profiling may add cost to the online inference hot path.
design_rationales.causal_mechanism: Separating or reusing profiling can avoid repeated measurement during execution.
design_rationales.alternatives_tradeoffs: Per-sample online profiling may adapt better but adds latency; offline profiling may fail to generalize.

design_rationales.concrete_problem: Uniform token retention ignores layer-wise redundancy and modality preferences.
design_rationales.causal_mechanism: Layer/modality-aware allocation can preserve budget for sensitive representations while compressing redundant ones.
design_rationales.alternatives_tradeoffs: Fixed layer ratios are simpler and reproducible; adaptive profiling adds cost and possible distribution-shift risk.

design_rationales.concrete_problem: Modality-local importance may remove tokens needed for cross-modal semantics.
design_rationales.causal_mechanism: A cross-modal alignment cue may retain tokens carrying interaction-relevant information.
design_rationales.alternatives_tradeoffs: Attention-only or diversity selection may be cheaper but biased; alignment scoring adds undefined compute.

design_rationales.concrete_problem: Retraining or fine-tuning increases deployment cost.
design_rationales.causal_mechanism: Inference-time token selection can reuse original model weights.
design_rationales.alternatives_tradeoffs: Training-free deployment is easier but may provide weaker task-specific adaptation.
